questiontext.text:
We have simulated data sets giving the crop yield for different crops. The outcome variable is the Crop Yield, and the explanatory variables are:

  • Soil Quality Index Score - a numerical variable ranging from 1-10, representing soil quality, where higher scores indicate better quality.
  • Crop Planted - a factor variable indicating the type of crop planted.
  • Region - a factor variable specifying the region.
  • Density of pests in the crop - a numerical variable indicating the density of pests in the crop.
  • Pest susceptibility - a factor variable with three levels (low, medium, high) representing how susceptible the given crop is to pests.

The following visualisation shows the crop yield on the \(Y\) axis and the Soil Quality Index on the \(X\) axis. There are then two other dimensions built up from “aesthetics”, here: colour and size.

---

The Goal

We're trying to understand what affects crop yield (how much crop is produced) using a simulated dataset. We're looking at how soil quality, crop type, and pest susceptibility might impact how much crop we get.

---

How it works

In this plot, we use aesthetics (like position, color, and size) to map variables in the data onto parts of the plot. Here's how this one is structured:


Visual Element What It Represents
X-axis Soil Quality Index Score (1 to 10)
Y-axis Crop Yield (how much crop is grown)
Color Type of crop planted (Corn, Rice, Sorghum)
Size of dots Pest density (larger = more pests)


So each dot represents one observation (i.e., a crop planted in a field with a certain soil quality and pest density).

Interpreting the Plot

Let's translate what the plot is telling us visually:

  • Soil Quality vs Crop Yield: Generally, as you move right (higher soil quality), you often see the dots higher up (higher yield). This hints that better soil leads to more crop yield (a positive correlation).
  • Pest Susceptibility (Size): Bigger dots represent higher pest susceptibility. You'll notice that larger dots often appear lower on the Y-axis, suggesting higher pest susceptibility might reduce yield. Hence, pest problems might be hurting the crops.
  • Crop Type (Colour): The colours (gold, black, blue) represent different crops. The vertical spread of each colour looks similar, suggesting that crop type doesn't seem to make a big difference to yield in this plot.

---

Your Task

Download this data set. This is not the same as the data used to make the graphic above. Using the downloadable data, create a similar visualisation.
